title: Why do you want to join THIS company specifically?
shortTitle: Why do you want to join THIS company specifically?
keyPoints: Give researched, company-specific reasons that could not be pasted onto any other company.
Reference concrete things: their product, engineering blog, a public talk, a known technical decision.
Connect each company-specific reason to a specific career goal of yours for a two-way fit.
Cover multiple buckets: product and mission, scale and technical challenge, culture, and growth.
Avoid generic flattery like 'you are a great company' with no substance behind it.
Show that you treated this interview as a priority, not one of many identical applications.
A two-way match: they get your skills, you get the growth and mission you want.

s1_definition.oneliner: Give researched, company-specific reasons that could not be pasted onto any other company, tied to your own career goals.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Specificity from research** – Reference concrete facts about the company: their product, tech stack, engineering blog, recent news.
- **Two-way fit** – Connect each company-specific reason to a goal of yours, making it mutual value, not flattery.
- **Multiple buckets** – Cover product and mission, scale and challenge, culture, and career growth.
- **Impossible to recycle** – The answer should mention something only this company does, so it cannot be copied to another interview.
- **Priority signal** – Show that you invested real time researching this company, not just applying broadly.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Rajesh choosing where to invest his savings. A generic reason is "I want good returns" : true of every bank. A specific reason is "I am choosing National Bank of India because your real-time UPI settlement is the fastest in the market and I want my business payments to clear instantly." The second shows he actually studied the options.

sections.s6_takeaway:
I want to join this company specifically because of what you are building at National Bank of India and the fact that it maps exactly onto where I want to take my career. You are moving your core banking onto an event-driven architecture with real-time UPI settlement, and you run an in-house fraud platform at a scale of tens of millions of transactions a day. That is not a generic reason : it is specific to you.

I have deliberately been steering toward real-time payments and fraud. Your real-time settlement and your fraud platform are precisely that domain, at a scale that most places simply do not have. So this is a genuine two-way fit: I get to work on the specific problems I want to specialize in, and I can contribute immediately because I already bring hands-on payments experience.

I also looked at how you work as an engineering organization : your emphasis on ownership and your approach to incidents : and that matches how I like to operate. I want to own systems end to end and be accountable for them in production, and that is clearly the culture here.

The reason I answer this way is that this question is really testing whether I have done my homework and whether my motivation is real. So I give reasons that could not be copy-pasted onto any other company, I tie each specific thing about you to a specific goal of mine, and I show that I can contribute from day one.

Remember one sentence: Give company-specific reasons tied to your career goals that prove you researched this company and cannot recycle this answer anywhere else.
